New raw `raw/stripe-payments-satispay-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-satispay-accept-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-satispay-accept-payment.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/satispay/accept-a-payment`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 base capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/satispay/accept-a-payment (new raw lines 5-20) identifies Satispay acceptance and links Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents, Direct API, iOS and Android. It provides no integration prerequisites, payment steps or state transitions. The May 8, 2026 detailed guide (old raw lines 12-49 and 95-130) describes redirect-based single-use EUR payment, customer authorization, immediate outcome notification, and same-currency lines for eligible Checkout payment sessions without setup or subscription modes. In the May Payment Intents flow the merchant server creates the Intent and the client confirms with a return URL (old raw lines 799-934). In Direct API the client uses Stripe.js confirmPayment with the Intent client secret and return URL. A distinct manual redirect option starts with server-side Intent confirmation and takes the customer through requires_action and next_action.redirect_to_url. Return is followed by checking Intent status, and completion is eligible for webhook-driven fulfillment (old raw lines 1268-1362). In the manual-capture path, successful authentication and authorization precede requires_capture and a subsequent capture call (old raw lines 1094-1140). source-stripe-satispay-accept-payment.md lines 13-31 retain the overall modes and capture window but misassign Direct API confirmation to a server-side confirmSatispayPayment function and overstate both platforms' custom-scheme requirements.
reviewed_answers.Q2: The change at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/satispay/accept-a-payment is presentational/navigation only. New raw lines 9-20 replace detailed bodies with six variant routes, so the missing prose supplies no evidence of removed features, renewed prerequisites, or deprecation. The behavior in source-stripe-satispay-accept-payment.md remains anchored to the May 8, 2026 full capture, including the same-currency and payment-mode limits, Dashboard recommendation versus manual configuration, seven-day manual-capture window with cancellation if unused, and sandbox test approval/decline versus live redirect (old raw lines 12-49, 564-568 and 1094-1158). Separately correct summary lines 23-25 and the corresponding Stripe Wallets route: the May Direct API uses client-side Stripe.js confirmPayment and optionally server-side paymentIntents.confirm for manual redirect (old raw lines 1268-1356), iOS offers either a custom URL scheme or universal link for automatic dismissal, and the Android sample uses PaymentLauncher without stating a custom scheme (old raw lines 1565-1603 and 1804-1853). Preserve the root-to-Stripe-index route, the provider's source route, and the Wallets-to-source link (wiki index line 7, Stripe index lines 385 and 414, Wallets line 426). Add the source-to-Wallets link and distinguish the November navigation locator from May behavioral provenance. On May 8, 2026, the acceptance guide's Checkout and Elements/Checkout Sessions compatibility tables limit Satispay to payment mode and explicitly exclude setup and subscription modes (old raw lines 18-35 and 95-113). Separately, the May 8 overview records recurring payments No (raw/stripe-satispay-2025.md lines 28-30) and lists Subscriptions among products where the Dashboard can add Satispay (lines 98-105). The related overview summary lines 21-23 and Wallets concept lines 319-327 should identify this evidence boundary. The Dashboard mention is not evidence that Satispay funds recurring charges. The generic Android sample's mandate/future-use comment (old raw lines 1836-1846) supplies no affirmative Satispay recurring support.
